events.summary: Morgan Tsvangirai was brutally beaten in custody, and images of his battered and swollen face became world news.
Morgan Tsvangirai heads the larger faction of the Movement for Democratic Change and has emerged as a strong challenger in this year's election.
A faction of Zimbabwe's MDC led by Tendai Biti says it has suspended Morgan Tsvangirai as party leader, a move Tsvangirai's faction dismisses as unconstitutional and meaningless.
Morgan Tsvangirai's two-year-old grandson Shawn drowned in the pool at his Harare home, a fortnight after his wife Susan was killed in a car crash.
Morgan Tsvangirai withdrew from Zimbabwe's presidential runoff election.

Morgan Tsvangirai ended a three-week tour of the US and Europe in France, during which his appeals for aid and investment met suspicion and caution, and he raised about $200 million, short of his $700 million to $1 billion target.

Zimbabwean Prime Minister Morgan Tsvangirai said he had been the victim of a smear campaign over his private life after he was forced to cancel his high-profile wedding because a judge ruled he was customarily married to another woman.
Morgan Tsvangirai was suspended by the MDC's national council after a meeting instigated by Tendai Biti.

Susan Tsvangirai, wife of Zimbabwe's prime minister Morgan Tsvangirai, was killed at age 50 when a seven-ton aid truck struck their four-wheel-drive vehicle; Morgan was hospitalized with head and neck injuries before being flown to Botswana.

Morgan Tsvangirai accused African Union observation mission head Nkosazana Dlamini-Zuma of distorting his complaints of vote-rigging and questioned her integrity as an impartial observer ahead of Zimbabwe's election.
Morgan Tsvangirai was sent to hospital for medical check-ups after arriving for a court hearing with a deep head wound and walking with a limp following his arrest over the weekend.
Morgan Tsvangirai is introduced as Zimbabwe's prime minister at a power-sharing signing ceremony, calling the agreement a product of a painful compromise.
Morgan Tsvangirai is under intense pressure to form a government of national unity with Robert Mugabe, but he rejects talk of such a government until Mugabe steps down.
Morgan Tsvangirai rejects a SADC resolution proposing that his MDC share control of Zimbabwe's home affairs ministry with Robert Mugabe's Zanu-PF in a unity government.
Morgan Tsvangirai was detained by police at a roadblock near Kwekwe while campaigning for the June 27 presidential run-off, the third time he had been detained since returning to Zimbabwe.
Morgan Tsvangirai pulled out of Zimbabwe's presidential run-off election, calling it a violent, illegitimate sham of an election process.
Morgan Tsvangirai appeared in court on the first of two treason counts, part of an ongoing trial on charges he plotted to kill President Robert Mugabe in late 2001.
Morgan Tsvangirai was unable to attend a meeting of regional leaders in Swaziland aimed at breaking Zimbabwe's power-sharing deadlock because the state would not grant him a passport.

Zimbabwe's opposition party accuses the military of deploying 18 snipers in a plot to kill Morgan Tsvangirai, which the MDC says is the principal reason he has not returned to Zimbabwe to campaign for the June 27 runoff.
Prime Minister Morgan Tsvangirai summoned security ministers to demand an immediate return to the rule of law, following the arrest of his deputy minister Roy Bennett.

A senior government source says Morgan Tsvangirai won 47% of Zimbabwe's presidential vote to Robert Mugabe's 43%, indicating a run-off would be needed since Tsvangirai did not reach the 50% threshold for an outright victory.

Zimbabwe opposition leader Morgan Tsvangirai is in South Africa to increase pressure on Robert Mugabe to release the result of the presidential election held 10 days ago, and to admit defeat or hold a clean run-off vote.
Zimbabwe's opposition Movement for Democratic Change announced that Morgan Tsvangirai had won enough votes to secure the presidency outright, while official presidential results remained unannounced.
Morgan Tsvangirai, after his defeat in Zimbabwe's presidential election, gave his biggest hint yet that a popular uprising is the only option left for resisting Robert Mugabe's regime.
Morgan Tsvangirai predicted he would win the long-delayed election run-off with President Robert Mugabe if it is fair, as Zimbabwe's electoral commission set the run-off for June 27, 2008.
Morgan Tsvangirai decides to pull out of Friday's presidential run-off in Zimbabwe.

Early election results in Zimbabwe show President Robert Mugabe leading opposition leader Morgan Tsvangirai, with 27,065 votes to Tsvangirai's 15,621 in the central Midlands and southern Matabeleland South provinces.

Morgan Tsvangirai rejects Zimbabwe election result.

Morgan Tsvangirai was brutally beaten in custody, and images of his battered and swollen face became world news.

Zimbabwe opposition leader Morgan Tsvangirai was seriously injured by police and arrested along with more than 110 activists during an anti-government demonstration in Harare.
Morgan Tsvangirai returns to Harare for talks on the unimplemented power-sharing agreement and to discuss whether his party should withdraw from the proposed national unity government.

Morgan Tsvangirai delayed his return to Zimbabwe after a credible source reported a planned assassination attempt against him.
